commands.review_summary:
The PR removes active-turn exceptions from LLM-boundary inbound-metadata stripping and updates boundary/cache-stability tests to expect active user text to match historical stripped text.

PR surface: Source +1, Tests +110. Total +111 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level. Current main keeps active inbound metadata while stripping it after the turn ages into history, and this patch's own changed path shows active metadata would now be removed before provider conversion.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Contributor or maintainer follow-up is needed to revise the prompt-context shape and add inspectable real behavior proof; automation should not take over while the external proof gate is unmet.

target.title: fix(agents): strip inbound metadata from the active user turn too, for byte-stable prompt caching
target.body:
Fixes #100271

**Reported-by:** @Peetiegonzalez
**cc:** @Peetiegonzalez

### Problem

The channel layer decorates the ACTIVE user message with a "Conversation info (untrusted
metadata)" / "Reply target of current user message (untrusted, for context)" block, but the
session store only ever persists the bare (already-stripped) text.
`stripHistoricalInboundMetadataFromUserMessages`
(`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.ts`) already strips this block from
historical user turns before replay, but left the active turn's block in place. The active turn
is what becomes the PREVIOUS turn's history the moment a new turn arrives, so its serialized bytes
changed retroactively at that point in the conversation on every single turn — invalidating any
prefix/exact-match provider prompt cache from there onward, every turn. Full details and
evidence in #100271.

(#90811 fixed the *timestamp* half of this same active/historical asymmetry; this is the
remaining half — the metadata block itself.)

### Fix

`stripHistoricalInboundMetadataFromUserMessages` now strips inbound metadata from the active turn
identically to a historical turn, in all three text shapes it handles:
- **Envelope-wrapped** (`[DOW YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ...] ` channel envelope, or a cron
  "Current time:" marker): the envelope is still preserved verbatim; only the metadata block
  behind it is stripped, active or historical.
- **Plain text** (no envelope): stripped then stamped from the message's own timestamp, same as
  historical.
- **Multi-block (attachment) turns**: the second-and-later text blocks are metadata-stripped
  regardless of active/historical, same as the first block already was via the envelope/plain
  path.

The `isActive` branch that special-cased "return raw unchanged" / "keep the block" for the active
turn is removed from all three call sites; `isActive` is still used elsewhere in the function
(the current-turn timestamp-override matching), so it isn't removed entirely.

### Measurements

| Config | TRUE cache hit% (gpt-5.5, ChatGPT-OAuth, 12-turn identical-prompt A/B, session-affinity
header from #100233 already applied) |
|---|---|
| stock (active keeps metadata) | 81.8% |
| + this fix | **90.6%** |

Anthropic (claude-sonnet-4-6) shows the larger effect on the write side, since its cache matches
only at explicit `cache_control` breakpoints: stock, the mutated active-turn byte voids everything
past the 36,105-token system-prompt breakpoint every turn, so the whole conversation tail gets
rewritten into the cache each turn at the 1.25x cache-write rate. With this fix, over a 12-turn
session: **cacheWrite 60,208 -> 10,051 tokens (-83%)**; cacheRead advances monotonically instead
of resetting to the same breakpoint every turn.

DeepSeek and Kimi (incremental/multi-prefix caches) mostly absorb the mutation already (95.4% vs
93.9%, and 89.7% vs 96.0% respectively) — this fix is neutral-to-slightly-positive there, not a
regression. Full per-model tables in #100271.

### Trade-off

The active turn no longer surfaces its own message_id/sender/reply-target JSON inline to the
model (same strip as a historical turn always had). The equivalent patch has been running as a
dist hot-patch on a production OpenClaw gateway since 2026-07-04 (real traffic soak) with no
observed regressions in reply threading, mentions, or routing.

### Tests

`attempt.llm-boundary.cache-stability.test.ts`: 3 new tests asserting the active-turn form is
byte-identical to its later historical form for (a) an envelope-wrapped message, (b) a
non-enveloped message, (c) the second text block of a multi-block (attachment) turn.

`attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`: updated 3 existing tests that encoded the old "active turn keeps
its metadata" behavior as the intended spec — they now assert the metadata is stripped from the
active turn too (byte-identical to history), matching the new intended behavior. All other tests
in this file were unaffected (their "current turn" fixtures carried no metadata to begin with).

Typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`) clean — output byte-identical
before/after (42 pre-existing, unrelated `ui/` module-resolution errors on this branch, confirmed
present on unmodified upstream main too).

Full `unit-fast` vitest shard (`test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts`, which is where this test
file actually runs — see note below) passes clean: 11,000 passed / 10 failed / 4 skipped, and the
10 failures are byte-identical (same 5 files, same test names) to the failures already present on
unmodified upstream main before this change — i.e. zero regressions introduced by this diff.

Note: this test file is dynamically routed into the `unit-fast` shard rather than the
`agents-embedded-agent` shard by content-based classification
(`test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast-paths.mjs`), not a static per-file config — worth knowing if a
future PR touching this file sees "No test files found" against the more obvious-looking shard.
